A Function answers three practical questions:
What input does it operate on?
Raw text, vector representations or retrieved candidate results.
Vector embeddings used for retrieval, or reordered results returned to the user.
From a workflow perspective, Functions participate in search in two distinct stages:
: Functions run before search to convert text into vector representations. These vectors determine which candidates are retrieved.
: Functions run after candidate retrieval to refine the ordering of results without changing the candidate set.

Pre-search Functions: Convert text to vector embeddings
run before candidate retrieval. Their role is to convert raw text—both stored documents and incoming queries—into vector representations that the search engine uses to identify relevant candidates.
Different Pre-search Functions generate different types of embeddings, which directly affects how retrieval is performed.

All Pre-search Functions are applied consistently to both document data and query text, ensuring retrieval is performed within the same representation space.
